page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The two shells
lines: The cell wall forms two thin overlapping shells.
The upper shell is the epitheca; the lower
They fit together as the two halves of a
steps.why: The wall is in two unequal halves: the larger epitheca overlaps the smaller hypotheca the way a lid closes over its box — the syllabus states this with the soap box comparison.
common_mistakes: Swapping the names. Epi- means upon, so the epitheca is the upper, overlapping shell.
Writing a single continuous wall. The two-shell structure is the point being tested.
steps.memory_tip: Epi- = upon (upper lid); hypo- = below (lower box).
steps.margin_note: Both shell names plus the soap box line carry this mark.

steps.label: Silica wall
lines: The walls are embedded with silica,

lines.text: Two silica shells: epitheca over hypotheca.

steps.why: Silica makes the wall resist decay; this is why diatom walls pile up on the sea floor as diatomaceous earth.
common_mistakes: Writing cellulose or chitin. The wall material tested here is silica.
steps.memory_tip: Silica is the substance; indestructible is the property — write both words.
steps.margin_note: Silica and indestructible are the two marked words.

insider_note: Four words carry this answer: epitheca, hypotheca, soap box and silica — write all four.
